newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mixed, yen sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mixed, yen sharply lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed as the U.S.-Iraqi confrontation kept December yen pinned to the lower end of the day's ranges, traders and analysts said.

"The U.S. and Iraqi confrontation seemingly added pressure to the yen," said Michael Malpede, currency analyst at Refco Inc, adding that the situation in the Middle East could raise crude oil prices and further pressure yen futures.
December yen set a contract low at $0.009186 amid heavy volume. Volume in December yen was estimated at 27,000, with spread activity being the main feature in the pit, they said.
On Wednesday the Pentagon said the U.S. was now moving F-117A stealth fighters and B-52 bombers near Iraq in apparent preparation for new strikes against President Saddam Hussein's military.
In the morning, the Pentagon said Iraqi forces had fired one or two missiles at U.S. warplanes over northern Iraq.
December yen could fall to $0.009122, which is roughly equivalent to the dollar/yen's yearly high at 111.15 spot.
Traders also attributed comments from Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, for yen's declines.

Sakakibara said there was no specific target for the dollar level against the yen and also embellished Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer's strong-dollar comments. Sakakibara said Tietmeyer's comments were favourable for Japan.
"Sakakibara's comments opened the door for a speculative assault," Malpede said.

While yen futures held near the bottom of its daily range for most of the day, marks and Swiss francs gravitated off its highs late. The dollar/mark bounced above the 1.5100 spot level as pit trade was ending after U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin reiterated support for a strong dollar.

Analysts said the mark was supported by underlying concerns about the European Monetary Union. Concerns re-emerged on talk that the French budget, which will be released on September 18, will be higher than expected, analysts said.
"Traders had jumped on Tietmeyer's comments, but the dynamics in Europe haven't improved," an analyst said.

December marks set their daily high at $0.6682, above the pivot point of $0.6678, soon after the opening, but edged towards its daily low of $0.6662 late in the day. December mark volume was estimated at 21,000 contracts, while volume for December Swiss francs was at 16,000.

One trader noted that a large U.S. bank offered 2,000 December Canadian dollars at $0.7323 in the all-or-nothing pit. However, the bank pulled the offer from the all-or- nothing pit, which only accepts orders above 100 lots.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000037 at $0.009196, marks up $0.0007 at $0.6666, Swiss francs up $0.0012 at $0.8175, sterling up $0.0006 at $1.5554, Canadian dollars were down $0.0004 at $0.7320 and Austalian dollars were down $0.0006 at $0.7971.
